subject: Anchoring proposal for private stack — staggered platform fee + premium SRE option
messages:
From: Paige Lin <paige@brightwave.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Commercial ask: amortize platform fee & SRE add-on

Thanks for the call earlier. A couple of follow-ups from our procurement/finance team — we need the commercial items in writing so we can run this through our CFO. High level asks: 

- Amortize the upfront private deployment/platform fee across 24 months (we prefer a straight-line approach) rather than treating it as an upfront lump sum.
- Offer a discounted premium SRE add-on (24/7 on-call + 2x quarterly architecture reviews). Target discount: ~20% off standard SRE list.
- Pilot: can we get a 3-month pilot credit (we'll commit to a 12-month min after pilot if metrics look good).
- Exit liability: limit to 3 months of platform fee instead of 6 — our procurement team is sensitive about long tail liabilities.

Attached the internal commercial matrix (Brightwave_MA_proposal.xlsx) and a short note on our expected node counts. Please include any SOC2/attestation clause language and redline guidance.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Paige Lin
Head of Platform, Brightwave Health
paige@brightwave.com

Marissa / Laura — forwarding Brightwave's note (below). Quick context: they ran the numbers after yesterday's architecture review and want to anchor amortization to 24 months + a 20% SRE discount. Deal: BW-2026-0910-01; expected initial private deployment: US east region; pilot start target first week of Nov. 

Primary asks for pricing:
- Can we amortize the platform fee over 24 months? If so, what's the P&L impact (and any conditions)?

- Pilot credit: they asked for 3 months; we typically offer a pilot credit but need to decide size.
- Exit cap: they want 3 months. Current legal suggests 6 months standard.

Notes: they will push for minimal up-front cash to preserve runway. We can propose partial amortization or a blended approach tied to usage floors. Laura — any constraints from finance on amortizing platform fees? Marissa — please propose a counter that preserves minimum committed economics while addressing their cash concern.

Thanks,
Aditya

Subject: Re: Fwd: Commercial ask: amortize platform fee & SRE add-on

Aditya — thanks for the context. I sketched a counter that balances customer cash needs and our revenue recognition / risk profile. Summary below; I kept the language conservative with clear triggers.

Proposed counter (high level):
- Platform fee amortization: allow amortization over 12 months (instead of 24) with the following conditions:
  * Amortization only applies if customer signs a 12-month minimum committed usage floor (we model this as a GAAP-friendly deferral schedule).
  * If they meet >90% of the usage floor in months 9–12, remaining balance recognized; otherwise we accelerate to standard recognition and bill difference.
- Pilot credit: provide a 3-month pilot credit capped at $25k (applies to platform fee only). Pilot converts to a 12-month commitment at the end of the pilot to enable amortization.
- SRE premium: offer a 15% discount on list SRE retainer for year 1 (24/7 coverage + 2 architecture reviews / quarter). Standard pricing returns in year 2 unless they convert to a multi-year SRE contract.
- Exit liability: reduce to 3 months of platform fee (as requested) but require a 60-day notice and a migration assistance SOW if they exercise it.
- Legal & SOC2: provide standard SOC2 attestation clause; any evidence beyond the standard will be charged as an add-on professional services item.

Rationale: 12-month amortization gives them cash relief while limiting our GAAP exposure. The pilot credit and usage floor protect us from churn and ensures meaningful adoption.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Aditya: run the 12-month amortization math with finance (Laura) and confirm cap sizing for pilot credit.
2) I will draft a short commercial term sheet (1 page) and a redline for SOW; we can attach Brightwave_SOW_v2.pdf and send to Paige.
3) If they accept, route to legal for a narrow addendum covering amortization triggers.

Attachments: none yet — I'll prepare the term sheet today.

-Marissa
Head of Commercial Pricing
Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Anchoring proposal for private stack — staggered platform fee + premium SRE option

Paige — thanks for flagging these items and for the clear priorities. After reviewing internally, here's a pragmatic counter we can put on the table to help your CFO and procurement team move forward.

Counter-offer (commercial highlights):
- Platform fee amortization: we can support an amortization schedule over 12 months (straight-line) subject to a 12-month minimum committed usage floor. This reduces your up-front cash while keeping recognition rules straightforward.
- Pilot credit: 3-month pilot credit capped at $25,000, applied to the platform fee; pilot must convert to the 12-month minimum commitment for amortization to apply.
- SRE premium: we will provide a 15% discount on our premium SRE retainer for year 1 (includes 24/7 on-call, two architecture reviews per quarter). After year 1, SRE reverts to standard list pricing unless you elect a multi-year SRE commitment.
- Exit liability: we will cap early termination liability to the equivalent of 3 months of platform fee, with a requirement for 60 days notice and a migration assistance SOW (we can scope that separately).
- SOC2 & attestation: standard SOC2 report available. Any bespoke evidence requests beyond our standard package will be handled via an add-on professional services engagement.

I've attached the updated SOW (Brightwave_SOW_v2.pdf) with the amortization language in section 2.3 and a short 1-page term sheet summarizing the above. If this looks acceptable, I can send a DocuSign for the term sheet + SOW and loop in legal for the narrow amortization addendum.

Proposed next steps:
1) Review this counter internally and let me know where we are aligned.
2) If acceptable, we'll issue DocuSign by EOD tomorrow and schedule a 30-minute sign-off call.

Thanks again — want to keep this simple for your CFO.

Best,
